title: No hay + sustantivo + que no: una afirmación universal

sections.content: No hay + noun + que no + subjunctive ("there is no X that doesn't...") is a double negative that reads as a sweeping universal claim -- the strongest way to say "every single one" without literally saying it, perfect for a closing lesson arguing that Cold War polarization touched absolutely everything. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: No hay institución política que no se viera obligada, tarde o temprano, a definirse frente a esta confrontación global.
items.english: There is no political institution that wasn't eventually forced to take a stance on this global confrontation.

items.spanish: No hay universidad latinoamericana de este periodo que no experimentara las mismas tensiones ideológicas que dividían al resto de la sociedad.
items.english: There is no Latin American university from this period that didn't experience the same ideological tensions dividing the rest of society.

items.spanish: No hay prácticamente ningún sindicato obrero de la región que escapara a esta misma dinámica.
items.english: There is practically no labor union in the region that escaped this same dynamic.

items.spanish: No hay ejército latinoamericano de este periodo que no acabara adoptando algún elemento de la Doctrina de Seguridad Nacional.
items.english: There is no Latin American military from this period that didn't end up adopting some element of the National Security Doctrine.

sections.content: The verb inside the que clause is always subjunctive here, since the sentence is describing a category ("any X") rather than one specific, known thing -- que no se viera, que no experimentara, que no acabara, all in the subjunctive.
